hold harmless Client and its affiliates, directors, officers, employees and agents

elements.element: Third-party claims alleging services/deliverables infringe IP
elements.evidence: (i) an allegation that the Interface, the Hosting Services, the Support Services or any deliverable furnished by TrueLink infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right

elements.evidence: (ii) TrueLink's breach of any applicable law, rule or regulation

(iv) TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct

elements.evidence: a. Client shall indemnify and hold TrueLink ... arising from or relating to the following: (list not reproduced; unchanged by the redline)

elements.element: Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications)
elements.evidence: no obligation under clause (i) to the extent the claim arises from Client Content or from Client's unauthorized modification or combination of the Interface

elements.element: IP remedies: procure, modify, replace, refund
elements.evidence: No remedy mechanic appears anywhere in the inserted clause c.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity subject to super-cap of 3× annual fees
elements.evidence: Inserted text contains no cap; comment only says 'we can discuss a super-cap'.

reasons: The inserted clause c. delivers every Vendor-side element of the preferred position: defend/indemnify, Customer plus affiliates, IP infringement of the Interface/Hosting Services/Support Services/deliverables, Vendor breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and notice/control/cooperation procedure.

The preferred position's final limb — limiting Client's own indemnity at 12.a to Client-provided content and Client's breach of law — was not addressed; clause 12.a remains an open 'arising from or relating to the following' indemnity of TrueLink and its licensors whose enumerated triggers are not visible, so the limitation cannot be confirmed as met. A short 'solely to the extent arising from Client Content or Client's breach of applicable law' insertion in 12.a would close the preferred level.
Fallback is not independently satisfied (no procure/modify/replace/refund remedy and no 3× annual fees super-cap), but the locked target is preferred, so this is not a defect in itself.

Minimality holds: a concise insertion for an absent vendor indemnity, with narrow customary carve-outs; existing 12.b (broader breach indemnity in our favour) is left intact and clause c. is expressly 'Without limiting the foregoing'.
Note that clause c. relies on 'Client Content' and 'Client Confidential Information'; confirm both are defined terms elsewhere in the agreement to avoid a dangling reference.
